executive_assessment.text: Named vulnerability examples include Zvimba crops, Sanyati service access and water-point pressures primarily in Masvingo/Matabeleland South/Midlands, all explicitly dated.
Mwenezi, Chipinge and Makoholi provide concrete reported adaptation/governance inputs; their outcomes are not independently evaluated.
Protection risks and stakeholder climate-security pathways remain qualitative assessments rather than measured climate-caused violence.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2024-05 reports: The appeal documents a February 2024 dry spell exceeding 30 days; its cover caption identifies wilting, prematurely maturing maize in Zvimba District.
Source dated 2024-12 reports: UNICEF reported 6,028 water points broken and 2,310 identified sources dry in 2024, primarily in Masvingo, Matabeleland South and Midlands provinces.

Source dated 2024-12 reports: A UNICEF outreach in Sanyati identified a severely malnourished seven-year-old; her family lived 38 km from the nearest clinic, and the report says drought-related food insecurity and disrupted facility access left children vulnerable.

Source dated 2025-03-19 reports: In drought-prone Mwenezi, Pikinini Jawanda lead farmer Chizivano Shava combines runoff trenches, infiltration pits, rainwater capture and two tanks totaling 130,000 litres; his wife reports less distant water collection and enough for household and garden use.

Source dated 2026-09-17 reports: The September 2026 mission reported that Pikinini-Jawanda's 156-hectare scheme supports 300 farmers from 12 villages; farmers diversified crops and maintained production and financial records to manage the shared investment.

Source dated 2026-09-17 reports: UNDP reports expansion of Vimbanayi from 23 to 35 hectares with improved water abstraction, storage and conveyance; a scheme leader said farmers now produce maize, chilli, sugar beans and vegetables with more income streams.

Source dated 2026-09-17 reports: At Makoholi, 15 Farmer Field Schools and 56 demonstration plots directly reach 330 farmers and share learning with about 1,500 others; 188 extension officers have trained in fodder harvesting and feed formulation.
